title.zh: 卷13 列傳第5 文閔明武宣諸子
title.en: Volume 13 Biographies 5: Princes of Wen, Xiaomin, Wu, and Xuan
title.raw: 卷13 列傳第5 文閔明武宣諸子 Volume 13 Biographies 5: Princes of Wen, Xiaomin, Wu, and Xuan

sentences.zh: 文閔明武宣諸子

translations.literal: Princes of Wen, Xiaomin, Wu, and Xuan
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Wen, Emperor Xiaomin, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan

sentences.zh: 文帝十三子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen (Yuwen Tai) had thirteen sons.

sentences.zh: 姚夫人生世宗，後宮生宋獻公震，文元皇后生孝閔皇帝，文宣皇后叱奴氏生高祖、衛剌王直，達步干妃生齊王憲，王姬生趙僭王招，後宮生譙孝王儉、陳惑王純、越野王盛、代奰王達、冀康公通、滕聞王逌。

translations.literal: Consort Yao bore Shizong; the rear palace bore Duke of Song Xian Zhen; Empress Wen Yuan bore Emperor Xiaomin; Empress Wen Xuan, the Chilu clan, bore the High Ancestor and Prince of Wei Zhi; Consort Tabghan bore Prince of Qi Xian; a royal lady bore Prince of Zhao Zhao; the rear palace bore Prince of Qiao Xiao Jian, Prince of Chen Huo Chun, Prince of Yue Ye Sheng, Prince of Dai Yi Da, Duke of Ji Kang Tong, and Prince of Teng Wen You.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yao bore Shizong; ladies of the rear palace bore Duke of Song the Exalted Zhen; Empress Wen Yuan bore Emperor Xiaomin; Empress Wen Xuan of the Chilu clan bore Yuwen Yong (the future Emperor Wu) and Prince of Wei the Impetuous Zhi; Consort Tabghan bore Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian; a royal lady bore Prince of Zhao the Presumptuous Zhao; the rear palace bore Prince of Qiao the Filial Jian, Prince of Chen the Bewildered Chun, Prince of Yue the Wild Sheng, Prince of Dai the Proud Da, Duke of Ji the Peaceful Tong, and Prince of Teng the Cultivated You.

sentences.zh: 齊煬王別有傳。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi the Flamboyant has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi the Flamboyant (Yuwen Xian) has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 衛剌王直，字豆羅突。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei the Impetuous Zhi, styled Douluotu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei the Impetuous Yuwen Zhi, styled Douluotu.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，封秦郡公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was enfeoffed Duke of Qin commandery, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei (556), he was enfeoffed Duke of Qin commandery with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成初，出鎮蒲州，拜大將軍，進衛國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he went out to command Pu Province, was appointed grand general, advanced to Duke of Wei state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wucheng era (559), he went out to command Pu Province, was appointed grand general, and advanced to Duke of Wei with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 保定初，為雍州牧，尋進位柱國，轉大司空，出為

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was governor of Yong Province; soon advanced to pillar-of-state, transferred to grand minister of works, and went out as
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he was governor of Yong Province; soon advanced to pillar-of-state, transferred to grand minister of works, and went out as

translations.literal: (Liang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Liang]

sentences.zh: 〔襄〕州總管。

translations.literal: [Xiang] Province commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: commander-in-chief of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 天和中，陳湘州刺史華皎舉州來附，詔直督綏德公陸通、大將軍田弘、權景宣、元定等兵赴援，與陳將淳于量、吳明徹等戰於沌口。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era, Chen Xiangzhou governor Hua Jiao raised the province to submit; an edict ordered Zhi to supervise Suide Duke Lu Tong, grand generals Tian Hong, Quan Jingxuan, Yuan Ding, and others' troops to go to aid, and they fought Chen generals Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others at Dun mouth.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe (566–572), Chen Xiangzhou governor Hua Jiao brought his province over to Zhou; an edict ordered Yuwen Zhi to supervise Suide Duke Lu Tong, grand generals Tian Hong, Quan Jingxuan, Yuan Ding, and others in marching to the relief, and they fought Chen generals Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others at Dun mouth.

sentences.zh: 直軍不利，元定遂投江南。

translations.literal: Zhi's army was unfavorable; Yuan Ding then defected to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi's army fared badly; Yuan Ding then defected to the south.

sentences.zh: 直坐免官。

translations.literal: Zhi was punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi was dismissed from office as punishment.

sentences.zh: 直高祖母弟，性浮詭，貪狠無賴。

translations.literal: Zhi was the younger brother of the emperor's elder grandmother's line; by nature he was frivolous and deceitful, greedy and ruthless, without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi was a younger brother on the emperor's grandmother's side; by nature he was frivolous and deceitful, greedy and ruthless, and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 以晉公護執政，遂貳於帝而昵護。

translations.literal: Because Duke of Jin Hu held the government, he then turned against the emperor while drawing close to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the government, he sided against the emperor while currying favor with Hu.

sentences.zh: 及沌口還，慍於免黜，又請帝除之，冀得其位。

translations.literal: When he returned from Dun mouth, he was angry at being dismissed; he also asked the emperor to remove Hu, hoping to obtain his position.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from Dun mouth, he resented his dismissal; he also urged the emperor to remove Hu, hoping to take his place.

sentences.zh: 帝夙有誅護之意，遂與直謀之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long harbored intent to execute Hu; he then plotted with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long intended to kill Yuwen Hu; he then plotted with Yuwen Zhi.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，帝乃以齊王憲為大冢宰。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, the emperor then made Prince of Qi Xian grand minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was executed, the emperor made Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian grand minister of war.

sentences.zh: 直旣乖本望，又請為大司馬，意欲總知戎馬，得擅威權。

translations.literal: Zhi, having missed his original hope, again requested to be grand marshal, intending to oversee all military affairs in general and wield authority at will.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi, disappointed in his original ambition, again asked to be made grand marshal, intending to command all military affairs and wield power at will.

sentences.zh: 帝揣知其意，謂之曰：「汝兄弟長幼有序，寧可反居下列也？

translations.literal: The emperor guessed his intent and said to him: "You brothers have an order of seniority and juniority—how could you turn and stand below in rank?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor perceived his intent and said to him: "You brothers have an order of senior and junior—how could you willingly rank below?

sentences.zh: 」乃以直為大司徒。

translations.literal: " He then made Zhi grand minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made Yuwen Zhi grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以直第為東宮，更使直自擇所居。

translations.literal: Initially the High Ancestor had given Zhi's residence as the Eastern Palace; he had Zhi choose his own dwelling anew.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Yuwen Yong had assigned Yuwen Zhi's residence as the Eastern Palace and had him choose another dwelling.

sentences.zh: 直歷觀府署，無稱意者，至廢陟屺佛寺，欲居之。

translations.literal: Zhi went through all government offices and found none to his liking; arriving at the abandoned Siji Buddhist temple, he wished to live there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi toured the government compounds and found none satisfactory; coming to the abandoned Siji Buddhist temple, he wished to live there.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲謂直曰：「弟兒女成長，理須寬博，此寺褊小，詎是所宜。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian said to Zhi: "Younger brother, your sons and daughters are grown; by reason they need spacious quarters—this temple is cramped; how is it suitable?
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian said to him: "Younger brother, your children are grown; they need room—this temple is cramped; how can it be suitable?

sentences.zh: 」直曰：「一身尚不自容，何論兒女！

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "One body cannot even accommodate itself—what talk of sons and daughters!
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Zhi said: "I can hardly fit myself—what of children!

sentences.zh: 」憲怪而疑之。

translations.literal: " Xian was astonished and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was startled and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 直嘗從帝校獵而亂行，帝怒，對衆撻之。

translations.literal: Zhi once followed the emperor on a hunting review and went out of line; the emperor was angry and flogged him before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi once followed the emperor on a hunt and broke formation; the emperor was angry and had him beaten before the company.

sentences.zh: 自是憤怨滋甚。

translations.literal: From then resentment and anger grew ever more.
translations.idiomatic: From then his resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸雲陽宮，直在京師，舉兵反，攻肅章門。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Yunyang Palace, Zhi was in the capital and raised troops in rebellion, attacking Suzhang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Yunyang Palace, Yuwen Zhi was in the capital, raised troops in revolt, and attacked Suzhang Gate.

sentences.zh: 司武尉遲運閉門拒守，直不得入。

translations.literal: Director of Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun closed the gate and held defense; Zhi could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Martial Affairs Yuchi Yun shut the gate and held it; Yuwen Zhi could not enter.

sentences.zh: 語在《運傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Yun."
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the "Biography of Yuchi Yun."

sentences.zh: 直遂遁走，追至荊州，獲之，免為庶人，囚於別宮。

translations.literal: Zhi then fled; pursued to Jing Province, he was captured, demoted to commoner, and imprisoned in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhi then fled; pursued to Jing Province, he was captured, reduced to commoner status, and imprisoned in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 尋而更有異志，遂誅之，及其子賀、貢、塞、響、賈、秘、津、乾理、乾璪、乾悰等十人，國除。

translations.literal: Soon he again harbored different intent; he was then executed, together with his sons He, Gong, Sai, Xiang, Jia, Mi, Jin, Qianli, Qianbao, Qiancong, and ten others in all; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he showed further treasonous intent; he was executed together with his sons He, Gong, Sai, Xiang, Jia, Mi, Jin, Qianli, Qianbao, Qiancong, and ten others in all; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，加招等殊禮，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui assisted the government, he added extraordinary honors for Zhao and others: they need not hurry in court audience and might wear sword and shoes in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian (later Emperor Wen of Sui) directed the government, he granted Zhao and others extraordinary honors: they need not quicken their step at court and might enter the hall with sword and shoes.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝將遷周鼎，招密欲圖之，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to shift Zhou's mandate, Zhao secretly wished to plot against him to restore the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was about to seize the Zhou throne, Zhao secretly plotted against him to save the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 乃邀隋文帝至第，飲於寢室。

translations.literal: He then invited Emperor Wen of Sui to his residence and drank with him in the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Yang Jian to his mansion and entertained him in the bedroom.

sentences.zh: 招子員、貫及妃弟魯封、所親人史冑，皆先在左右，佩刀而立。

translations.literal: Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan and his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, together with his intimate Shi Zhou, were all beforehand at his side, wearing swords and standing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's sons Yuan and Guan, his consort's younger brother Lu Feng, and his confidant Shi Zhou stood by with swords drawn.

sentences.zh: 又藏兵刃于帷席之間，後院亦伏壯士。

translations.literal: He also hid weapons among the curtains and bedding; in the rear courtyard brave men lay in ambush as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also hid weapons in the curtains and bedding, and posted strong men in the rear courtyard.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝從者多在合外，唯楊弘、元冑、冑弟威及陶徹坐於戶側。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui's attendants were mostly outside the compound; only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou, Zhou's younger brother Wei, and Tao Che sat by the door.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Yang Jian's attendants waited outside; only Yang Hong, Yuan Zhou, Zhou's younger brother Wei, and Tao Che sat beside the door.

sentences.zh: 招屢以佩刀割瓜啖隋文帝，隋文帝未之疑也。

translations.literal: Zhao repeatedly used his girdle knife to cut melon and feed Emperor Wen of Sui; Emperor Wen of Sui did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao repeatedly cut melon with his belt knife and offered it to Yang Jian, who suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 元冑覺變，扣刀而入。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhou sensed something amiss, knocked his knife and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhou sensed danger, struck his blade, and entered.

sentences.zh: 招乃以大觴親飲冑酒，又命冑向廚中取漿。

translations.literal: Zhao then personally drank to Zhou with a great goblet and also ordered Zhou to go to the kitchen for broth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then personally offered Zhou a large cup of wine and ordered him to the kitchen for broth.

sentences.zh: 冑不為之動。

translations.literal: Zhou did not stir for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou did not move.

sentences.zh: 滕王逌後至，隋文帝降階迎之，元冑因得耳語曰：「形勢大異，公宜速出。

translations.literal: Prince of Teng You arrived afterward; Emperor Wen of Sui descended the steps to welcome him, and Yuan Zhou thus got to whisper in his ear: "The situation is greatly changed—you should leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Teng You arrived later; Yang Jian went down the steps to greet him, and Yuan Zhou whispered: "Everything has changed—you must leave at once.

sentences.zh: 」隋文帝共逌等就坐，須臾辭出。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen of Sui with You and the others took seats; after a little while he excused himself and went out.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jian sat briefly with You and the others, then excused himself and left.

sentences.zh: 後事覺，陷以謀反。

translations.literal: Later the affair was discovered; he was framed on a charge of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later the plot was discovered; he was charged with treason.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，誅招及其子德廣公員、永康公貫、越攜公乾銑、弟乾鈴、乾鏗等，國除。

translations.literal: That autumn he executed Zhao together with his sons Duke of Deguang Yuan, Duke of Yongkang Guan, Duke of Yuexie Qianxian, younger brothers Qianling and Qianheng, and others; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yang Jian executed Zhao together with his sons Duke of Deguang Yuan, Duke of Yongkang Guan, Duke of Yuexie Qianxian, and younger brothers Qianling and Qianheng; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 招所著文集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Collected writings by Zhao in ten scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's collected writings in ten scrolls circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 冀康公通，字屈率突。

translations.literal: Duke of Ji the Peaceful Tong, styled Qushuotu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Ji the Peaceful Yuwen Tong, styled Qushuotu.

sentences.zh: 武成初，封冀國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 天和六年十月，薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianhe, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianhe (571), he died.

sentences.zh: 子絢嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), the heir was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 大象中，為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Daxiang (579–581), he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝一男。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaomin had one son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaomin had one son.

sentences.zh: 陸夫人生紀厲王康。

translations.literal: Lady Lu bore Prince of Ji the Stern Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu bore Prince of Ji the Stern Yuwen Kang.

sentences.zh: 紀厲王康，字乾定。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji the Stern Kang, styled Qianding.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ji the Stern Yuwen Kang, styled Qianding.

sentences.zh: 保定初，封紀國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 仍出為總管利始等五州、大小劍二防諸軍事、利州刺史。

translations.literal: He then went out as commander-in-chief of Lishi and four other provinces, the two defenses of Greater and Lesser Sword, and all military affairs, and governor of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out as commander-in-chief of Lishi and four other provinces, the defenses of Greater and Lesser Sword, and all related military affairs, and as governor of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 康驕矜無軌度，信任僚佐盧奕等，遂繕脩戎器，陰有異謀。

translations.literal: Kang was arrogant and without measure, trusting his aides such as Lu Yi; he then repaired weapons of war and secretly harbored different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was arrogant and lawless, trusting aides such as Lu Yi; he repaired weapons and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 司錄裴融諫止之，康不聽，乃殺融。

translations.literal: Recorder Pei Rong remonstrated and stopped him; Kang would not listen and then killed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Pei Rong remonstrated with him; Kang refused to listen and killed Rong.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔賜康死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered Kang to die by grant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande (575), an edict granted him death.

sentences.zh: 子湜嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大定中，為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: In the Dading era, he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Dading (581), he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 明帝三男。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming (Yuwen Yu) had three sons.

sentences.zh: 徐妃生畢剌王賢，後宮生酆王貞、宋王寔。

translations.literal: Consort Xu bore Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian; the rear palace bore Prince of Feng Zhen and Prince of Song Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xu bore Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian; ladies of the rear palace bore Prince of Feng Zhen and Prince of Song Shi.

sentences.zh: 畢剌王賢，字乾陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian, styled Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bi the Impetuous Yuwen Xian, styled Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，封畢國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was enfeoffed Duke of Bi state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding (564), he was enfeoffed Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史，遷荊州總管，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Hua Province, was transferred to Jing Province commander-in-chief, and advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Hua Province, was transferred to commander-in-chief of Jing Province, and advanced to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 宣政中，入為大司空。

translations.literal: In the Xuanzheng era, he entered office as grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuanzheng (578), he entered office as grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 大象初，進位上柱國、雍州牧、太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state, governor of Yong Province, and grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang (579), he advanced to senior pillar-of-state, governor of Yong Province, and grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣帝崩。

translations.literal: The next year, Emperor Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Xuan (Yuwen Yun) died.

sentences.zh: 賢性強濟，有威略。

translations.literal: Xian by nature was forceful and resolute, with authority and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was forceful and resolute, with authority and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 慮隋文帝傾覆宗社，言頗泄漏，尋為所害，幷其子弘義、恭道、樹孃等，國除。

translations.literal: Fearing that Emperor Wen of Sui would overturn the ancestral temple, his words leaked somewhat; soon he was killed by him, together with his sons Hongyi, Gongdao, and Shuniang, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yang Jian would overthrow the dynasty, he let his views slip; soon he was killed, together with his sons Hongyi, Gongdao, and Shuniang; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 酆王貞，字乾雅。

translations.literal: Prince of Feng Zhen, styled Qianya.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Feng Yuwen Zhen, styled Qianya.

sentences.zh: 初封酆國公。

translations.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Feng state.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Feng.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 大象初，為大冢宰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was grand minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang (579), he was grand minister of war.

sentences.zh: 後為隋文帝所害，幷子濟陰郡公德文，國除。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Jiyin commandery Dewen; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Jiyin Dewen; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 武帝生七男。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu (Yuwen Yong) had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 李皇后生宣帝、漢王贊，厙汗姬生秦王贄、曹王允，馮姬生道王充，薛世婦生蔡王兌，鄭姬生荊王元。

translations.literal: Empress Li bore Emperor Xuan and Prince of Han Zan; Consort Kuhan bore Prince of Qin Zan and Prince of Cao Yun; Lady Feng bore Prince of Dao Chong; Lady Xue bore Prince of Cai Dui; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Jing Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li bore Emperor Xuan and Prince of Han Zan; Consort Kuhan bore Prince of Qin Zan and Prince of Cao Yun; Lady Feng bore Prince of Dao Chong; Lady Xue bore Prince of Cai Dui; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Jing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 漢王贊，字乾依。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Zan, styled Qianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yuwen Zan, styled Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 初封漢國公。

translations.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Han state.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王，仍柱國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince, still pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince while remaining pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 大象末，隋文帝輔政，欲順物情，乃進上柱國、右大丞相。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, Emperor Wen of Sui assisted the government and, wishing to accord with popular sentiment, advanced him to senior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang (581), Yang Jian directed the government and, wishing to placate opinion, advanced him to senior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 外示尊崇，寔無綜理。

translations.literal: Outwardly showing honor and esteem, in truth there was no overall governance.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was honored; in fact he held no real authority.

sentences.zh: 及諸方略定，又轉太師。

translations.literal: When the various regions were settled, he was again transferred to grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was pacified, he was transferred to grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 尋為隋文帝所害，幷其子淮陽公道德、弟道智、道義等，國除。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Huaiyang Daode and younger brothers Daozhi and Daoyi; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Huaiyang Daode and younger brothers Daozhi and Daoyi; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 道王充，字乾仁。

translations.literal: Prince of Dao Chong, styled Qianren.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dao Yuwen Chong, styled Qianren.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，封王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, he was enfeoffed prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande (577), he was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 蔡王兌，字乾俊。

translations.literal: Prince of Cai Dui, styled Qianjun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cai Yuwen Dui, styled Qianjun.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，封王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, he was enfeoffed prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande (577), he was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 荊王元，字乾儀。

translations.literal: Prince of Jing Yuan, styled Qianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jing Yuwen Yuan, styled Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，封王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was enfeoffed prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng (578), he was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 元及兌、充、允等竝為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: Yuan together with Dui, Chong, Yun, and the rest were all killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan together with Dui, Chong, Yun, and the others were all killed by Yang Jian; their fiefs were abolished.

sentences.zh: 宣帝三子。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had three sons.

sentences.zh: 朱皇后生靜皇帝，王姬生鄴王

translations.literal: Empress Zhu bore Emperor Jing; a royal lady bore Prince of Ye
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhu bore Emperor Jing (Yuwen Chan); a royal lady bore Prince of Ye

translations.literal: (Yan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yan]

sentences.zh: 〔衎〕，皇甫姬生郢王術。

translations.literal: [Kan], and Lady Huangfu bore Prince of Ying Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, and Lady Huangfu bore Prince of Ying Shu.

sentences.zh: 鄴王

translations.literal: Prince of Ye
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ye

translations.literal: (Yan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yan]

sentences.zh: 〔衎〕，大象二年，封王。

translations.literal: [Kan]; in the second year of Daxiang, he was enfeoffed prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Kan; in the second year of Daxiang (580), he was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 郢王術，大象二年，封王。

translations.literal: Prince of Ying Shu; in the second year of Daxiang, he was enfeoffed prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ying Shu; in the second year of Daxiang (580), he was enfeoffed as prince.

sentences.zh: 與

translations.literal: Together with
translations.idiomatic: Together with

translations.literal: (Yan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yan]

sentences.zh: 〔衎〕並為隋文帝所害，國除。

translations.literal: [Kan] they were all killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Kan they were all killed by Yang Jian; their fiefs were abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔賢之議者，咸云以周建五等，歷載八百；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In olden days those who discussed worthies all said that Zhou established the five ranks and lasted eight hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: In olden days commentators all said that Zhou established the five ranks of nobility and endured eight hundred years;

sentences.zh: 秦立郡縣，二世而亡。

translations.literal: Qin established commanderies and counties and perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Qin established commanderies and counties and fell in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 雖得失之迹可尋，是非之理互起，而因循莫變，復古未聞。

translations.literal: Though the traces of gain and loss can be traced, the reasoning of right and wrong rises in turn, yet following precedent none changed, and restoring antiquity was not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Though one can trace the record of gain and loss, and arguments over right and wrong alternate, custom never changed and no one sought to restore antiquity.

sentences.zh: 良由著論者溺於貴達，司契者難於易業，詳求適變之道，未窮於至當也。

translations.literal: Truly because those who set forth theories were drowned in esteem for the eminent, and those who held the tally found it hard to change their trade—the way of seeking what fits change was not exhausted to the utmost of fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because theorists were beholden to the eminent, and officials clung to established practice—the art of adapting institutions to the times was never pursued to its proper end.

sentences.zh: 嘗試論之：

translations.literal: Let us try to discuss it:
translations.idiomatic: Let us try to discuss it:

sentences.zh: 夫皇王迭興，為國之道匪一；

translations.literal: Sovereigns and kings rise in succession; the way of establishing a state is not one alone;
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns and kings rise in succession; the way to found a state is not single;

sentences.zh: 賢聖間出，立德之指殊塗。

translations.literal: the worthy and sage appear in turn; the aim of establishing virtue takes different paths.
translations.idiomatic: worthies and sages appear in turn; the aim of establishing virtue takes different paths.

sentences.zh: 斯豈故為相反哉，亦云治而已矣。

translations.literal: How could this be deliberately made opposite? It is also said: to govern—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is not deliberate contradiction—it is simply governance.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 五等之制，行於商周之前；

translations.literal: The system of five ranks operated before Shang and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: The system of five ranks operated before Shang and Zhou;

sentences.zh: 郡縣之設，始於秦漢之後。

translations.literal: the establishment of commanderies and counties began after Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: the establishment of commanderies and counties began after Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 論時則澆淳理隔，易地則用舍或殊。

translations.literal: Judging the times, then decadence and purity are separated in principle; changing the place, then use and rejection may differ.
translations.idiomatic: Times differ, so decadence and purity are worlds apart; circumstances differ, so what is adopted or abandoned may vary.

sentences.zh: 譬猶干戈日用，難以成垓下之業；

translations.literal: It is like arms used daily—hard to accomplish the enterprise below the ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: It is like using arms daily—hard to accomplish the enterprise of Gaixia;

sentences.zh: 稷嗣所述，不可施成周之朝。

translations.literal: what Jisi set forth cannot be applied in the court of accomplished Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: what Jisi (Sima Qian) set forth cannot be applied in the court of accomplished Zhou.

sentences.zh: 是知因時制宜者，為政之上務也；

translations.literal: Thus to adapt measures to the times is the supreme task of governing;
translations.idiomatic: Thus adapting measures to the times is the supreme task of governing;

sentences.zh: 觀民立教者，經國之長策也。

translations.literal: observing the people to establish teaching is the long strategy of ordering the state.
translations.idiomatic: observing the people to establish teaching is the long strategy of ordering a state.

sentences.zh: 且夫列封疆，建侯伯，擇賢能，置牧守，循名雖曰異軌，責實抑亦同歸。

translations.literal: Moreover, demarcating territory, establishing marquises and earls, selecting the worthy and able, setting governors and defenders—by name it is called a different track, but in demanding reality it likewise returns to one end.
translations.idiomatic: Demarcating territory, enfeoffing marquises and earls, selecting the worthy, appointing governors and defenders—by name the tracks differ, but in demanding real results they aim at the same end.

sentences.zh: 盛則與之共安，衰則與之共患。

translations.literal: In prosperity they share security with it; in decline they share calamity with it.
translations.idiomatic: In prosperity they share security; in decline they share calamity.

sentences.zh: 共安系乎善惡，非禮義無以敦風；

translations.literal: Shared security depends on good and evil; without ritual and righteousness there is no way to temper custom;
translations.idiomatic: Shared security depends on conduct; without ritual and righteousness custom cannot be tempered;

sentences.zh: 共患寄以存亡，非甲兵不能靖亂。

translations.literal: shared calamity rests on survival or extinction; without arms and armor disorder cannot be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: shared calamity rests on survival or extinction; without arms disorder cannot be stilled.

sentences.zh: 是以齊、晉帥禮，鼎業傾而復振；

translations.literal: Thus Qi and Jin led with ritual, and the tripod enterprise tilted yet revived;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qi and Jin led with ritual, and the royal enterprise tilted yet revived;

sentences.zh: 溫、陶釋位，王綱弛而更張。

translations.literal: Wen and Tao relinquished rank, and the royal net slackened yet was drawn tight again.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen and Tao Kan relinquished rank, and the royal framework slackened yet was drawn tight again.

sentences.zh: 然則周之列國，非一姓也，晉之群臣，非一族也，豈齊、晉強于列國，溫、陶賢於群臣者哉，蓋勢重者易以立功，權輕者難以盡節故也。

translations.literal: Then Zhou's feudal states were not of one surname, and Jin's ministers were not of one clan—were Qi and Jin stronger than the feudal states, and Wen and Tao worthier than the ministers? It was that heavy power is easy for establishing merit, and light authority is hard for fulfilling loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's feudal states were not of one surname; Jin's ministers were not of one clan—were Qi and Jin stronger than the other states, and Wen and Tao worthier than other ministers? Heavy power makes merit easy; light authority makes full loyalty hard.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，建侯置守，乃古今之異術；

translations.literal: From this speaking, establishing marquises and setting defenders are techniques of antiquity and the present that differ;
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that enfeoffing princes and appointing governors are techniques that differ between antiquity and the present;

sentences.zh: 兵權勢位，蓋安危之所階乎。

translations.literal: military authority, power, and position are surely the steps on which security and danger depend.
translations.idiomatic: military authority, power, and position are the steps on which security and danger depend.

sentences.zh: 太祖之定關右，日不暇給，旣以人臣禮終，未遑藩屏之事。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor settled Guanzhong, days allowed no leisure; having ended in the rites of a subject, he had no time for the screen of the feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai settled Guanzhong, he had no leisure; having died in the status of a minister, he had no time to enfeoff a princely screen.

sentences.zh: 晉蕩輔政，爰樹其黨，宗室長幼，竝據勢位，握兵權，雖海內謝隆平之風，而國家有磐石之固矣。

translations.literal: Jin the Reckless assisted the government and thereupon planted his faction; senior and junior of the imperial clan alike held power and position, grasped military authority—though within the seas the breeze of great peace was gone, yet the state had the solidity of bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu assisted the government and planted his faction; senior and junior of the imperial house alike held power and grasped military authority—though peace within the realm was gone, the state had the solidity of bedrock.

sentences.zh: 高祖克翦芒刺，思弘政術，懲專朝之為患，忘維城之遠圖，外崇寵位，內結猜阻。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor cut away thorns, thinking to expand governing arts, punishing the harm of monopolizing the court while forgetting the far plan of protecting the wall; outwardly he honored favored rank, inwardly he bred suspicion and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Yong cut away rivals, intending to improve governance, punishing court monopoly while forgetting the long-range plan of a princely bulwark; outwardly he honored rank, inwardly he bred suspicion.

sentences.zh: 自是配天之基，潛有朽壤之墟矣。

translations.literal: From then the foundation matching Heaven secretly had ground of crumbling ruin.
translations.idiomatic: From then the foundation that should match Heaven secretly held crumbling ruin.

sentences.zh: 宣皇嗣位，凶暴是聞，芟刈先其本枝，削黜遍於公族。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne; cruelty and violence were what was heard; he mowed down first the root branches and cut away throughout the public clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan succeeded; cruelty and violence were notorious; he mowed down the root branches of the clan and cut away the royal kin throughout.

sentences.zh: 雖復地惟叔父，親則同生，文能附衆，武能威敵，莫不謝卿士于當年，從侯服於下國。

translations.literal: Though again in territory they were the emperor's uncles, in kin they were born of the same womb, in civil matters able to win the multitude, in martial able to awe the enemy—none failed to yield ministerial rank in that year and follow marquis's garb in a lesser state.
translations.idiomatic: Though in title they were the emperor's uncles, born of the same house, able in civil matters to win followers and in martial to awe foes—all alike resigned high office and wore a lesser lord's dress.

sentences.zh: 號為千乘，勢侔匹夫。

translations.literal: Called a thousand chariots, in power they matched a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Titled lords of a thousand chariots, in power they were no more than commoners.

sentences.zh: 是以權臣乘其機，謀士因其隙，遷龜鼎速於俯拾，殲王侯烈于燎原。

translations.literal: Thus powerful ministers rode their opportunity, strategists exploited their gaps; moving the sacred tripod was swift as picking up what lay before one, extinguishing princes and kings fierce as a prairie fire.
translations.idiomatic: Thus powerful ministers seized their chance, strategists their openings; shifting the sacred tripod was swift as picking something up, and extinguishing princes fierce as a prairie fire.

sentences.zh: 悠悠邃古，未聞斯酷。

translations.literal: In remote deep antiquity such cruelty was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: In remote antiquity such cruelty was unheard of.

sentences.zh: 豈非摧枯振朽，易為力乎。

translations.literal: Was it not that withering the withered and shaking the rotten, change was easy in power?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not that withering the withered and shaking the rotten makes change easy?

sentences.zh: 向使宣皇采姬、劉之制，覽聖哲之術，分命賢戚，布於內外，料其輕重，間以親疎，首尾相持，遠近為用。

translations.literal: Had Emperor Xuan adopted the systems of Ji and Liu, surveyed the techniques of sages and worthies, assigned worthy kin and shared them within and without, gauged their weight and light, interspersed kin near and far, head and tail supporting each other, far and near serving as use—
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperor Xuan adopted the systems of the Zhou founders Ji Fa and Liu Lei, surveyed sage techniques, assigned worthy kin inside and outside the court, gauged their weight, mixed near and distant kin, head and tail supporting each other, far and near each serving a use—

sentences.zh: 使其勢位也足以扶危，其權力也不能為亂。

translations.literal: made their power and position sufficient to support peril, and their authority and power unable to make disorder—
translations.idiomatic: made their position enough to support the state in peril, and their power unable to make disorder—

sentences.zh: 事業旣定，僥倖自息。

translations.literal: when the enterprise was settled, lucky chances would of themselves cease.
translations.idiomatic: when the enterprise was settled, opportunists would of themselves cease.

sentences.zh: 雖使臥赤子，朝委裘，社稷固以久安，億兆可以無患矣。

translations.literal: Though one made an infant lie down and in the court entrusted the fur robe, the altars of soil and grain would be firmly long at peace, and the hundred millions could be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Though an infant lay on the throne and the court entrusted the fur robe, the altars would stand firm and the people be without fear.

sentences.zh: 何后族之地，而勢能窺其神器哉。

translations.literal: How could the ground of a empress's clan then have power to spy on the sacred vessel?
translations.idiomatic: How then could a consort's kin have power to seize the throne?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju (November 1971) edition of the Book of Zhou.
